key_insight: Compact MaxSAT encodings optimize idle-time balance first, then worst-case waiting, then total waiting, without sacrificing the optimal balance.
engineering_relevance: B2B scheduling systems can use this approach to reduce participant waiting while preserving meeting feasibility and explicit objective priorities.
method: Measure waiting as empty slots between each participant’s first and last meetings.
Lexicographically minimize idle range, maximum idle, and total idle; assess balance among participants requesting at least two meetings.
Compare Direct, Compact-Base, and Compact-Objective encodings, with proofs preserving feasible schedules, objective costs, and priorities.
evidence_signal: Tests covered 226 variants of 20 base instances with three repetitions per configuration; Compact-Objective had the lowest median clause count in all nine objective–dataset comparisons, and among 84 jointly optimal instances, selected lexicographic schedules reduced maximum idle on 11 and total idle on 56 versus selected range-only schedules.
watch_item: Smaller encodings did not consistently yield faster solving, and schedule-quality findings apply to subsets solved optimally under the compared objectives.
paper_title: Compact MaxSAT Encodings for Balanced Waiting in B2B Meeting Scheduling
